title: QBR Transition: Technical and Commercial Handoff Playbook
author: Priya Desai
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines a standardized cross-functional process for transitioning an enterprise customer from post-provisioning operations into a regular QBR (Quarterly Business Review) cadence. It focuses on a two-track handoff: (1) Technical handoff into steady-state SRE/Customer Success operations, and (2) Commercial handoff into Customer Success/Account teams for QBRs and renewed commercial commitments. The goal is to reduce post-go-live friction, ensure telemetry and SLO alignment, and provide a repeatable checklist for both technical and commercial stakeholders.

Scope and Intent:
- Applies to enterprise customers after successful go-live and the first 14 days of stability verification.
- Intended for customers using Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Covers telemetry gating, runbook ownership transfer, QBR readiness criteria, and obligations for escalation.

When to use this playbook:
1. After the 72-hour and 14-day stability sweeps complete and the customer is marked "operational" in the cutover checklist.
2. When the customer is expected to enter the first revenue-bearing QBR cycle or when an SLA/commercial review is requested.

Pre-handoff (Technical) Checklist - must be completed before commercial handoff:
1) Telemetry and Dashboards
   - Confirm tenant-specific dashboards exist in Grafana/Looker: "Tenant Overview", "Token Economics", "Model Quality Trends", "Latency & Errors".
   - Confirm synthetic journeys (happy path + edge cases) are running and passing for 14 consecutive days.
2) SLO and Alerting
   - SLOs validated: availability P99 >= 99.5% (for Dedicated) or SLA baseline met per contract.
   - Alert definitions and on-call rotation ownership documented and tested.
3) Security & Compliance Gates
   - Network controls (VPC peering, firewall rules) verified and recorded.
   - Logs retention and access review completed with security contact.
4) Operational Runbooks and Playbooks
   - Tenant runbook created: include common triage steps, known quirks, and rollback criteria.
   - Escalation contacts confirmed and smoke-test call executed.
5) Cost and Quota Protections
   - Billing alerts and quota caps configured; cost-protection webhook validated.

Roles and Responsibilities:
- Customer Success (CS): drive commercial handoff, coordinate QBR agenda, own account-level risks.
- SRE/Platform: own technical stabilization, SLO validation, and on-call readiness.
- Solutions Engineering (SE): provide architecture decisions, post-cutover optimizations, and model migration notes.
- Customer: confirm business objectives, authorized stakeholders for QBRs, and acceptance of operational telemetry.

Telemetry Gating Criteria (hard gates):
- Synthetic success rate >= 99% over 14d for primary flows.
- Observed token throughput within 20% of projected ramp for 7d or documented variance with mitigating plan.
- No P1 incidents in last 7d and P2 incidents trend stable or decreasing.

Technical Handoff Steps (numbered):
1. Finalize and publish tenant runbook to internal wiki; tag SRE on the page and mark as "owned".
2. Export tenant dashboards to the account folder and assign CS read-only links.
3. Run a joint smoke test between SRE, CS, and the customer that simulates these failure modes: model fallback, region failover, quota limit triggered.
4. Confirm on-call rotation contains a named owner for the tenant and verify escalation path to engineering.
5. Record the handoff meeting minutes with action items and owners in the ticketing system.

Commercial Handoff Checklist (concurrent with or after technical handoff):
- Confirm QBR cadence (quarterly by default) and primary agenda items: availability, cost/perf, model quality, roadmap alignment, risk and escalations.
- Prepare the Customer Health one-pager: activation metrics, synthetic pass rate, spend vs. forecast, open action items.
- Deliver a short technical appendix for the QBR: current model hosted, quantization profile, recent rollouts, and performance baselines.
- Agree on success metrics for the next quarter and an escalation SLA (response targets and review triggers).

Abort and Rollback Criteria (explicit stop conditions):
- Abort a commercial handoff if any hard telemetry gate fails (synthetic < 99% over 7d) or a P1 incident was recorded in the last 72h.
- Rollback model/route changes if model quality regression is above the agreed threshold: labeled false-positive rate increase > 4% or a decrease in mean quality score > 6 points on the evaluation harness.

Post-handoff Verification and QBR Triggers:
- Daily health digest for the first 14 days following handoff (email + Slack) summarizing synthetic pass rate, error budget burn, and cost delta.
- Trigger a Technical QBR (mini-review) if cost delta exceeds 25% of forecast or if SLO burn is > 30% in a 7d window.
- Add an item to the next QBR if any major action item remains open at handoff.

Standard QBR Agenda Template (recommended):
1) Executive summary (5m) - health and key asks
2) Operational review (15m) - availability, latency, incidents, SLO burn
3) Cost and capacity (10m) - spend trends, quota requests, committed units
4) Model quality (15m) - eval results, prompt regressions, A/B experiments
5) Roadmap and asks (10m) - upcoming migrations, dedicated capacity requests
6) Action items and owners (5m)

Sample alert thresholds and recommended dashboards (appendix table):
| Area | Metric | Threshold | Owner |
| Tenant Availability | P99 request latency | > 800 ms for 5m | SRE |
| Synthetic Journeys | Failure rate | > 1% over 15m | CS + SRE |
| Cost | Daily spend delta | > 25% above forecast | FinOps/CS |
| Model Quality | Eval pass delta | Drop > 4 points | SE/Research |

Operations examples and CLI snippets:
- Export synthetic test logs for a tenant (example):
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \ 
    "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tenants/{tenant_id}/synthetic-tests?from=2027-01-01&to=2027-01-15" 
    -o tenant-synthetics.json

- Example alert query (PromQL-like pseudo):
  rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{tenant_id="TENANT_123",le="0.8"}[5m]) < 0.95

Handoff meeting template (items to capture):
- Date/time, participants (roles), final telemetry snapshot, known risks, outstanding action items with owners and due dates, next QBR date.

Escalation alignment (who to call first):
1) Customer Success (primary commercial contact)
2) SRE on-call (technical P1/P2)
3) Solutions Engineering (architectural guidance)
4) Research/Model Onboarding (model regressions or quality escalations)

Reference materials and links:
- Tenant runbook template: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/tenant-runbook-template
- QBR slide template: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/health-and-qbr/qbr-template-and-operational-checklist-2026
- Escalation matrix: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook/urgent-escalation-handoff-and-sla-triage-2026

Appendix: common failure-mode playbooks to attach at handoff:
- Model fallback fanout and mitigation playbook (for heavy tail prompts)
- Quota surge and fair-share isolation playbook
- Observability mismatch triage checklist

Notes and best practices (guidance for teams):
- Keep the technical handoff independent of commercial readiness: do not finalize a QBR cadence until telemetry gates pass.
- Err on the side of shorter QBRs for the first two cycles: operational detail should be minimized in favor of clear action items.
- Keep dashboards minimal and focused: 4–6 widgets per dashboard for executives, 8–12 for technical owners.
